rows.why: Rule 1 on the disputed 21 cm link: the trail joining 19003 to the hot knot brightens cyan->green->yellow into the orange/dark-red stub ends (19008/19011/19012), i.e. it is coolest at 19003, so 19003 is the origin end and 19013 a stopping end; 19003 is also the deg-4 junction where the two long MIP arms (19002, 19018) come together.

Rule 1: deg-3 junction where the cyan MIP track from 16003 and the green/orange track to 16005 meet, with short stubs whose free ends go orange/red; both long arms brighten away from 16004, and it is the lower-z of the two junction candidates.
Rule 1 textbook: three prongs leave 13002 and every one gets hotter outward - dark red at 13001 and at 13003 (stopping protons) and an orange Bragg tip at the far end 13000 of the long track.

Rule 1: deg-4 knot carrying a dark-red short stub (proton, with 16006/16007 co-located) from which a MIP-level cyan/green track leaves toward the deg-1 dead end 16000; 16004 is also the lower-z end (z=68 vs 98).

Rule 1 + trap 2: the 10002 end shows a monotonic green->yellow->orange->dark-red rise into 10000 over the last ~10 cm (real Bragg stop, and 10003/10030/10000 are collinear track fragments, not prongs), so the cool cyan end 10001 - also far lower z (80 vs 195) - is the origin end.
Rule 1: deg-3 junction with a short orange->dark-red prong stopping at 15001 (proton) and a MIP cyan track leaving to 15000; both point away and 15002 is the lowest-z candidate.

The low-z end is multi-prong: 20008 is a deg-3 junction with stubs (20009, and 20010/20011 9 cm away) and a ~10 cm red proton prong (20001) hanging off the knot, while the long track stays MIP-cyan with only speckle to its exit at z=501 (no clean Bragg), so the vertex is the low-z knot and the muon goes forward in +z; rule 2 agrees.
Rule 8: the whole cluster is a single 4-cm dark-red stub with no readable direction - both ends are saturated red - so any candidate is as good as another; picked the deg-2, lower-z end.
Rule 1: two tracks leave this deg-2 kink and both end dark red (11004) and orange-red (11005) at their far ends, so both point away from 11076, which is also the lowest-z candidate.

Rule 1: kink vertex carrying a dark-red micro-stub (18077); the upper arm rises green->yellow->orange->dark red into 18000 (Bragg) and the lower arm also brightens toward 18001, i.e. every attached segment gets hotter away from 18002.

Rule 1: the single track rises monotonically cyan->green->orange->dark red into 17000 over the last several cm (clean Bragg stop at the 17002/17000 end), so the cool end 17001 is the origin; rule 2 agrees (z=3 vs z=100), though this looks like it could equally be an entry point at the upstream face.

Rule 1: at 5003 the track is cool cyan and carries two dark-red short stubs (5002/5025, proton-like), while the far end 5000 shows a clean green->yellow->orange->dark-red Bragg rise, so 5000 is the stop and 5003 the vertex; also 135 cm lower in z.
Rule 8: the entire cluster is a compact ~5 cm dark-red blob with no readable direction, so any of the four candidates is equivalent; picked the deg-3 junction at the centre.

Rule 1: deg-4 knot at the lowest-z end where the long MIP track (exiting at z=501) and a short prong that reddens to dark red toward 7006 both leave; the hot prong points away from 7010 and the muon stays MIP.
Rule 8: just a lot of scattered dots with no track or shower axis I can read, and the cluster's only two candidates are 3 mm apart, so the pick carries no information.
Rule 1: both arms get hotter away from the deg-2 junction 14002 - the long track ends dark red at 14001 and the short stub to 14000 is orange, while 14002 itself sits in the cool green part.

Rule 1: the single long track rises monotonically cyan->green->yellow->orange toward 8001, so 8001 is the Bragg stop; the cool end runs into the compact 8-cm blob of short segments and 8032 is the node the long track actually reaches (lowest z, so rule 2 agrees).

Rule 1: dQ/dx rises monotonically from dark blue at 9010 through green and yellow to dark red at 9004 over the whole 30 cm, so 9004 is the stop and 9010 is the cool end the track points away from; 9010 is also the lowest-z candidate (rule 2).
Rule 1 textbook: deg-3 hub 6003 with two short dark-red (several x MIP) stubs stopping at 6001 and 6004 plus a MIP-level track to 6000 - every attached segment is hotter away from 6003.

Rule 8-ish: one straight MIP track whose far end is at the x=-201 detector boundary and whose interior end carries a hot tip (looks like a stop, not a vertex); both candidates are the same point 2 cm apart, so I take the lower-z one and flag it as close to a guess.
Rule 1 + rule 3: deg-3 junction 13015 with a ~5 cm dark-red proton stub stopping at 13001 and a 140 cm muon running away to a dark-red Bragg end at 13000 - both point away from 13015.

Rule 1 with the two-Bragg trap in mind: deg-3 hub 16006 has prongs to a dark-red end at 16013/16007, to an orange/red end at 16009, and a MIP prong to 16000 - the junction both hot ends point away from; also the lowest-z hub node (rule 2).
Rule 1: deg-5 hub 23002 with a ~25 cm heavily-ionising arm that darkens to maroon at its far end 23000 plus several short stubs - everything radiates from 23002.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction 12001 with a short dark-red proton stub stopping at 12002 and a cooler MIP-level arm running to 12000; 12001 is also the lower-z of the two non-Bragg candidates (rule 2).

Two-Bragg-ends trap and I could not resolve it: the heavy track has a hot patch at its 11001 tip AND a sustained dark-red stretch just upstream of z~125, so I took the junction at z=125 (11017) where that heavy arm meets all the other short segments and the downstream EM cloud - but the profile is not monotonic to either end and 11001 as the shower apex is a live alternative.
Rule 1: the single ~11 cm segment rises to dark red at 9001 and is blue/cyan at the deg-3 node 9000, so 9001 is the stopping proton end and 9000 (where 9004 and 9015 also sit) is the vertex.

Rule 8 territory - a 3 cm object plus scattered grey dots; the only signal is yellow at 3001 darkening to red at 3000, which with rule 2 (3001 lower z) puts the vertex at 3001, but this is close to a guess.

The 180 cm track is uniform MIP with only a small orange/red patch at the 15006 end, so by rule 1 the cool 15008 end is the vertex; it is also 120 cm lower in z (rule 2) and has satellite charge around it.
Rule 1 + rule 3: the 185 cm track ends dark red at 13001 (stopping muon), so the vertex is the opposite, cool end where the deg-2 junction 13002 carries a short extra stub to 13000.
Rule 8 abstain: the cluster is disconnected grey fragments strung along the x=-200 anode with no readable trajectory, and the three candidates sit inside one ~7 cm blob - any click would be invented.
Rule 1: three-way junction whose every arm cools toward it - a dark-red stub rising to 84095, a track rising green->orange to a Bragg end at 84096, and a cool arm to the left.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction at lowest z with a short dark-red (proton-like) stub to 12001 on one side and a MIP track that warms to orange only at its far end 12000.
Rule 1 + degree: the long orange->dark-red track stops at 12013, and its cool end attaches to the bottom-left corner of the shower blob at the deg-5 vertex 12009.

Single 200 cm track; the 12000 end shows a graded green->yellow->orange->dark-red rise (Bragg stop) while 12001 has only one hot point, so 12001 is the start end - and it is also the lower-z end (rule 2).
A single 300 cm MIP track with no Bragg rise at either end; picked the deg-3 junction at the low-z (z~4 cm) end by rule 2, but nothing in the picture actually decides it.

Rule 1: the dark red belongs to the 5 cm stub 18003->18001 (proton-like, hotter away from the junction) while the 65 cm arm stays cyan/green right up to 18003 with no monotonic rise; the far end 18000 shows no Bragg only because it exits at the x~201 cm face, and 18003 is also the lower-z end.

Rule 8: the whole object is a ~5 cm compact blob of a few hot dots with no readable direction and all three candidates inside it, so any click is as good as any other - abstaining rather than inventing a reason.
Rule 1: deg-3 junction at the lowest z, with a 15 cm uniformly dark-red proton stub to 15003 on one side and a cool MIP track leaving to 15000 on the other - everything points away.

Two-Bragg-end case: hot at both ends with a cool green middle; the deg-2 junction 11001 at the low-z end carries the short dark-red stub to 11002 while the 90 cm MIP arm stops hot at 11000, so both arms point away from 11001.
Cluster 9 is a featureless MIP track with no Bragg rise; 9000 leaves at the x~201 cm face, so I picked the interior free end 9001, but this is close to a guess.

The long dark-red track stops at low z (8017/8001) and cools toward the blob, so the vertex is where it attaches at the lower-left edge of the dense region (deg-3 8037 at z~145); the blob itself is unreadable and ~6 candidates lie within 10 cm.
Rule 1: deg-4 vertex at the lowest-z end of the cluster carrying a 10 cm uniformly dark-red proton stub to 11009, while the main track leaves cool and only reddens ~60 cm away.
The 140 cm track exits at the y~-199 cm bottom boundary at 19000, so the interior, lower-z deg-2 end 19001 is the start; no Bragg anywhere makes this rule 2 plus geometry rather than rule 1.

Rule 1: the long track cools to blue as it approaches the deg-2 junction 7002 and rises monotonically to orange at the far end 7000 (Bragg stop), and a short dark-red proton stub runs from 7002 to 7001.

Same textbook pattern: cool blue arrival at the deg-2 junction 14003 with a short dark-red stub to 14001, and a monotonic green->orange->dark-red Bragg rise at the far end 14000; 14003 is also the lower-z end.

Rule 1 + trap note: the 230 cm track cools toward the low-z end and a short (7 cm) very hot stub hangs off the deg-2 junction 16002 there, so 16002 is the muon+proton junction and 16000 is the stopping end.
Single ~48 cm MIP-level track with two deg-1 ends and no readable Bragg rise; rule 2 tie-break only, 15001 is the lower-z end (z=455 vs 490).

One ~190 cm straight track, warm patches at both ends and no monotonic Bragg, so rule 1 is not decisive; 13000 sits on the bottom wall (y=-198) while 13001 is interior and at much lower z, so rule 2 decides.

Rule 1/6: the low-z end holds a multi-vertex complex with a ~12 cm uniformly dark-red (proton-like) stub to 8006, and the long track leaves it toward higher z; 8004 is the lowest-z deg-3 junction of that complex.

Rule 1 textbook: three segments leave 16004 and every one gets hotter away from it (dark-red short proton to 16001, and both longer prongs turn red at 16005 and 16000); 16004 is the deg-3 member of the co-located pair.

Rule 1: the long track rises from cyan to yellow toward the high-z end (so it stops there), and at the low-z end a short dark-red proton stub runs 15004->15001; 15004 is the deg-2 junction, also lowest z.

Rule 1: dQ/dx rises to dark red at 15003, so that end is the stopping end and the vertex is the cool end; among the three co-located candidates at z~147 I take the lowest-z deg-2 junction 15004 (coin flip with 15002).

Rule 1 over rule 2: 17001 is distinctly orange-red (Bragg/stopping) while 17000 is green, so the vertex is the cool end; but 17000 sits on the anode wall (x=-201) and the 370 cm single track looks cosmic, hence low confidence.

Rule 1: a ~20 cm uniformly red segment rises to dark red at 9001 (stopping proton) and a long MIP track runs from 9002 out to the downstream wall at z=500 (exiting, so no Bragg expected); 9002 is the deg-2 junction where they meet, at the lower z.

13002 is the only junction and the segment leaving it toward 13000 rises monotonically to dark red (Bragg stop), so 13000 cannot be the vertex; but the 13001 prong gets cooler going away (rule-1 violation) and 13001 sits ~10 cm off the anode, so a cosmic kinking at 13002 is a live alternative.

Rule 8 event - a compact hot spot with scattered grey dots and no readable direction - but all three candidates sit within 2 cm, so position is not in question; I take the deg-2 junction 16000 by the co-location convention.

Dense hadronic complex with no clean rule-1 reading; 8020 is the deg-5 junction near the centre and the dark-red stopping end at 8001 (z=305) points away from it, but several prongs cool going away, so this is close to a guess.

Rule 1: a single short heavily-ionising track whose dQ/dx rises monotonically from yellow at 17003 to dark red at 17000, so 17000 is the stop and the vertex is the cool low-z end 17003 (the deg-2 pair at z~349 is mid-track).

19001 is the deg-2 junction where both MIP segments meet and is at the lowest z; nothing is red anywhere, and the junction sits in the top-upstream corner (y=198, z=0) which smells cosmic, so only the id is confident, not the physics.

Rules 1+7: a short dark-red proton stub runs from the z~202 end up to its stopping point at 11009, and the shower opens out toward higher z from that same point; 11002 is the deg-3 candidate at the apex and the lowest-z candidate in the cluster.
